models_evaluated: eight automatic speech recognition systems (unnamed in abstract)

links.outcome: Effect of varying ASR transcription input on dementia classifier errors and biomarker values
links.effect: AUC 0.884 with human transcripts vs 0.870 for best ASR; ASR systems produced distinct false negative and false positive profiles and significantly altered linguistic biomarker magnitudes.
links.quote: These findings show that automated transcription does not simply introduce random noise into the speech-based assessment but it can systematically change clinical error profiles and biomarker estimates.

links.outcome: Whether aggregate AUC conceals differences in diagnostic error profiles across ASR systems
links.effect: Similar aggregate AUCs (best ASR 0.870 vs human 0.884) concealed distinct false negative and false positive profiles across ASR systems.
links.quote: However, similar aggregate ASR systems concealed clinically important differences in model behaviour.

unlisted_practices: Evaluate ASR components of speech biomarker pipelines on downstream clinical validity, diagnostic error, and biomarker preservation rather than transcription accuracy alone
